rationale.subject: Metro MAN
rationale.justification: Parameters validated: 800 hosts across 12 subnets, resiliency 'dual_homed', latency budget 5 ms.

rationale.subject: HQ <-> REMOTE-1
rationale.decision: OS2 SMF + 10GBASE-ER (Carrier EVPL (MEF E-Line) over provider OS2)
rationale.justification: Selected OS2 Single-Mode Fiber because link distance (22 km) exceeds the 400 m attenuation/dispersion limit of OM4 Multimode Fiber. Optical budget for 10GBASE-ER at 1550 nm: 22.0 km x 0.3 dB/km = 6.6 dB fibre + 1.5 dB connectors + 5 splices x 0.1 dB = 8.6 dB, + 1.0 dB safety margin = 9.6 dB <= 11.0 dB maximum channel insertion loss (headroom 1.4 dB). Rejected: 10GBASE-LR: reach 10 km < 22 km. The 10G optic is the UNI port speed; the purchased EVC CIR of 1 Gbps is enforced by an egress shaper on the router.

rationale.subject: HQ <-> REMOTE-2
rationale.decision: OS2 SMF + 10GBASE-ZR (Carrier EVPL (MEF E-Line) over provider OS2)
rationale.justification: Selected OS2 Single-Mode Fiber because link distance (35 km) exceeds the 400 m attenuation/dispersion limit of OM4 Multimode Fiber. Optical budget for 10GBASE-ZR at 1550 nm: 35.0 km x 0.3 dB/km = 10.5 dB fibre + 1.5 dB connectors + 8 splices x 0.1 dB = 12.8 dB, + 1.0 dB safety margin = 13.8 dB <= 23.0 dB maximum channel insertion loss (headroom 9.2 dB). Rejected: 10GBASE-LR: reach 10 km < 35 km; 10GBASE-ER: needs 13.8 dB > 11.0 dB budget. The 10G optic is the UNI port speed; the purchased EVC CIR of 1 Gbps is enforced by an egress shaper on the router.

rationale.justification: Ports are consumed by wired data/IoT/server endpoints and APs (250); 120 IP phones share the PC's port via the voice VLAN, so only port-consuming endpoints are counted. ceil(250 x (1 + 20% growth) / 24) = 13.

The distribution switch is pinned as root (priority 4096) so the L2 forwarding path matches the L3 gateway, and PortFast + BPDU Guard on edge ports stop a rogue switch from triggering a topology change.

rationale.justification: Although there are 4 sites, the carrier EVPL circuits are Layer-2 point-to-point Ethernet, so all routers form direct OSPF adjacencies as if on one campus. rationale.subject: Failure detection
rationale.decision: BFD 50 ms x 3 on WAN links + cost-based primary
rationale.justification: Dual-homed failover requires detecting a carrier fault faster than OSPF's 40 s dead interval. BFD (50 ms interval, multiplier 3) declares the neighbour down in 150 ms and triggers immediate SPF; primary circuits use OSPF cost 10 and secondary circuits cost 100 so traffic only shifts on failure.

rationale.subject: Latency budget
rationale.decision: Worst path REMOTE-1 -> HQ -> REMOTE-2 = 0.379 ms one-way (within 5 ms)
rationale.justification: Propagation in fibre is ~4.9 us/km (c / n with n ~ 1.47) plus a 0.05 ms forwarding allowance per hop. The worst site pair uses 7.6% of the 5 ms budget, so the remainder is reserved for queuing delay - which is why latency-sensitive classes get a strict-priority (LLQ) queue rather than relying on raw link speed.

rationale.subject: Failover latency
rationale.decision: Worst failover path HQ -> REMOTE-1 -> COLO = 0.345 ms (within 5 ms)
rationale.justification: Each primary circuit was removed in turn and the shortest surviving path recomputed (Dijkstra on latency). The worst case after a single failure still meets the budget, so dual-homing preserves the latency SLA, not just reachability.

rationale.subject: WAN edge QoS
rationale.decision: Hierarchical shaper + LLQ: REALTIME (DSCP EF, priority 30%), TRADING (DSCP AF41, 30%), MGMT (DSCP CS6, 5%)
rationale.justification: An EVPL is sold at a committed information rate, so the router first shapes to the CIR (otherwise the carrier polices excess and drops indiscriminately) and then queues inside the shaper: REALTIME uses the strict-priority LLQ to bound jitter and delay for sub-5 ms trading/voice flows, assured-forwarding classes get guaranteed minimum bandwidth, and class-default uses fair-queue. Traffic is marked by source subnet at the LAN ingress (wildcard-mask ACLs) so the classification is enforced at the trust boundary. IOS requires the shaper parent because CBWFQ cannot attach directly to a sub-interface.

rationale.subject: Packet-flow simulation
rationale.justification: Every LAN's last usable address was resolved by longest-prefix match to exactly one subnet (proves zero overlap), and representative flows (DHCP, DNS, Internet, lateral SMB, cloud MQTT/SSH) were walked through each generated ACL entry-by-entry using the same wildcard arithmetic the router applies.

[001] Metro MAN: metro profile, 4 sites, 5 links, root 172.16.0.0/16

== L1 Media ==============================================================
[002] HQ <-> REMOTE-1: OS2 SMF + 10GBASE-ER (Carrier EVPL (MEF E-Line) over provider OS2)
      Why: Selected OS2 Single-Mode Fiber because link distance (22 km) exceeds the 400 m attenuation/dispersion limit of OM4 Multimode Fiber. Optical budget for 10GBASE-ER at 1550 nm: 22.0 km x 0.3 dB/km = 6.6 dB fibre + 1.5 dB connectors + 5 splices x 0.1 dB = 8.6 dB, + 1.0 dB safety margin = 9.6 dB <= 11.0 dB maximum channel insertion loss (headroom 1.4 dB). Rejected: 10GBASE-LR: reach 10 km < 22 km. The 10G optic is the UNI port speed; the purchased EVC CIR of 1 Gbps is enforced by an egress shaper on the router.

[014] COLO access layer: 5 x 24-port access switch(es)

      Ref: IEEE 802.1Q (voice VLAN)
[015] Spanning tree: Rapid PVST+ (802.1w per VLAN), root at distribution
      Why: RSTP converges in under a second via proposal/agreement instead of 802.1D's 30-50 s listening/learning timers. The distribution switch is pinned as root (priority 4096) so the L2 forwarding path matches the L3 gateway, and PortFast + BPDU Guard on edge ports stop a rogue switch from triggering a topology change.
      Ref: IEEE 802.1w, IEEE 802.1D-2004
[016] Trunk policy: 802.1Q trunks, explicit allowed list, native VLAN 999, DTP off
      Why: Trunks carry only the VLANs that exist at that site (no 'allowed vlan all'), the native VLAN is moved to unused VLAN 999 and DTP is disabled with 'nonegotiate'. This blocks double-tagging VLAN hopping and switch-spoofing attacks; unused ports are shut down in black-hole VLAN 998.
      Ref: IEEE 802.1Q, Cisco SAFE

== Topology ==============================================================
[017] Topology tier: Dual-homed hub-and-spoke over carrier EVPL
      Why: Chosen because every remote site has diverse circuits to two hubs so the loss of one circuit or one hub never isolates a site.

== L3 Routing ============================================================
[036] Interior gateway protocol: OSPFv2 single area 0
      Why: Although there are 4 sites, the carrier EVPL circuits are Layer-2 point-to-point Ethernet, so all routers form direct OSPF adjacencies as if on one campus. The design is a single autonomous system with 21 subnets (< 50), so one LSDB stays small and SPF runs in milliseconds. A link-state protocol gives sub-second-to-seconds convergence without the hop-count limits and slow count-to-infinity behaviour of distance-vector RIP, and avoids the ABR/summarisation complexity that multi-area would add with no scaling benefit.
      Ref: RFC 2328 (OSPFv2)
[037] OSPF reference bandwidth: auto-cost reference-bandwidth 100000
      Why: The default 100 Mbps reference gives FastEthernet, 1G and 10G links the same cost (1). Raising it to 100 Gbps makes cost = 100000 / link Mbps, so 10G = 10, 1G = 100 and SPF prefers the faster path. Must be identical on every router.
      Ref: RFC 2328 Appendix C.3
[038] Failure detection: BFD 50 ms x 3 on WAN links + cost-based primary
      Why: Dual-homed failover requires detecting a carrier fault faster than OSPF's 40 s dead interval. BFD (50 ms interval, multiplier 3) declares the neighbour down in 150 ms and triggers immediate SPF; primary circuits use OSPF cost 10 and secondary circuits cost 100 so traffic only shifts on failure.
